extensions.question: Do the contracts and their validators survive this platform? Test UTF-8 with and without BOM, CRLF versus LF (the measured defect where the command-center validator hashes working-tree bytes and is therefore unrunnable on any Windows checkout), Windows reserved device names such as NUL and CON that break relative-path computation, long paths beyond 260 characters, and case-insensitive path collisions. Which validators break, and what is the minimal fix for each?

negative_controls.description: A raw CRLF digest of the same bytes must mismatch the LF blob; LF-normalised validators must stay silent on both states.

negative_controls.description: catalog.load must break on a UTF-8 BOM and succeed without one.

report.answer: Contracts ARC-0078/0080/0084 are absent on this tree. Live command-center digest validators SURVIVE CRLF vs the LF blob because they LF-normalise before hashing; a raw working-tree hash would still mismatch (the historical REACH-6 Windows defect). catalog.load, seed overlay, and unit_manifest receipts BREAK on a UTF-8 BOM (minimal fix: utf-8-sig). Reserved name NUL was created via the extended-length analogue and did not crash unit_manifest on Linux (Windows still needs an explicit refuse/prefix guard). Paths longer than 260 characters SURVIVE here (failure_mode=none-on-linux); Windows MAX_PATH remains unguarded. Case-insensitive collisions are not detected. SUCCESS:ARC-0106

findings.detail: ARC-0078, ARC-0080 and ARC-0084 contract files are not on this tree at command-center/phase4/contracts/. Conformance therefore targets the live command-center validators those contracts would bind (digest/manifest for ARC-0084; no plugin or packager module is present for ARC-0078/ARC-0080).
findings.minimal_fix: Author the three contract units; this report does not invent them.

findings.detail: validate.py REACH-6 and seed.py provenance hash LF-normalise before digesting. LF blob reach6_clean=True; CRLF working-tree reach6_clean=True; seed CRLF digest matches LF blob=True; unit_manifest and render_manifest match the LF-normalised digest. Naive raw CRLF digest would mismatch the blob (naive_would_break=True).
findings.minimal_fix: Keep read_bytes().replace(b'\r\n', b'\n') on every digest writer and reader. Do not hash working-tree bytes raw.

findings.detail: catalog.load uses encoding=utf-8 then json.loads, so a UTF-8 BOM raises. without_bom={'error': None, 'ok': True}; with_bom={'error': 'JSONDecodeError: Unexpected UTF-8 BOM (decode using utf-8-sig): line 1 column 1 (char 0)', 'ok': False}; unit_manifest BOM receipt ok=False (ManifestError: unreadable/unparseable JSON /tmp/arc0106-p1-7ga8urea/bom-lab/um-bom/command-center/receipts/BOM.json: Unexpected UTF-8 BOM (decode using utf-8-sig): line 1 column 1 (char 0)); seed overlay BOM ok=False (JSONDecodeError: Unexpected UTF-8 BOM (decode using utf-8-sig): line 1 column 1 (char 0)). json.loads under utf-8-sig accepts the same bytes.
findings.minimal_fix: Read JSON with encoding='utf-8-sig' (catalog.py, seed.py overlay, validate.py graph, unit_manifest receipts, register_parse.parse_file).

findings.detail: Created a file named NUL (Linux analogue of CreateFileW with the \\?\ prefix \\?\\\tmp\arc0106-p2-8meap8ed\reserved-lab\NUL). unit_manifest handled=True crashed=False relative_to={'crashed': False, 'ok': True, 'refused': False, 'relative': 'NUL'}. Live sources have no reserved-device guard; on Windows open('NUL') would bind the device rather than a file.
findings.minimal_fix: Reject path components whose stem is in {NUL,CON,PRN,AUX,COM1-9,LPT1-9} unless the caller used an extended-length prefix; never open the device.

findings.detail: Relative path length=336 absolute=378 created=True failure_mode=none-on-linux unit_manifest={'bytes': 14, 'crashed': False, 'ok': True, 'sha256': '44129124a7e038270c34e88133ba1b5da4cf40269866cf979964979698be2824'}. On this Linux host the path is legal. Windows without \\?\: FileNotFoundError / WinError 3 or 206 (filename or extension too long) once the path exceeds MAX_PATH=260 without \\?\.
findings.minimal_fix: On Windows, prefix paths at or above 260 characters with \\?\ before open/stat, or fail closed with an explicit path-too-long error.

findings.detail: Planted ['Manifest.json', 'manifest.json'] as distinct files (linux_distinct=2); casefold collisions={'manifest.json': ['Manifest.json', 'manifest.json']}. unit_manifest emitted 2 rows with 2 distinct digests. live_code_detects_casefold_collision=False.
findings.minimal_fix: When two registered paths compare equal under casefold, fail closed instead of treating them as distinct artifacts.

findings.detail: tools/plugin/validate.py and tools/package/boundary.py are not on this tree, so plugin-manifest interpreter rules and package exclusion/size-ceiling validators could not be executed. Path hostility was measured on the live digest/manifest tooling instead.
findings.minimal_fix: Deliver ARC-0078 and ARC-0080 validators, then re-run this suite.
